jurisdiction.name: Lebanon
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Lebanon has no AI-specific law or adopted national AI strategy. AI governance is being built by the Minister of State for Technology and Artificial Intelligence (MITAI), created in the 2025 government, whose LEAP roadmap (May 2025, updated March 2026) targets an 'AI-first government' by 2030 and proposes a Digital & AI Authority under the Prime Minister. The binding baseline is Law No. 81/2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data, whose Article 86 bars judicial or administrative decisions based solely on automated profiling. Sector bodies have issued AI guidance: CRDP's National AI Education Framework (2025) for schools and the Ministry of Public Health's Digital Health Vision (2023). The law creating MITAI, a Digital Authority law and a parliamentary proposal for a National AI Authority are pending, and MITAI's National AI Framework is under consultation without a published text.

narrative.review_notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. Parliament law database (lp.gov.lb) serves the full text of Law 81/2018; its 2024-2026 law lists contain no AI or digital law. Blocked or unreachable for automated reading: omsar.gov.lb (Cloudflare challenge; old /Assets PDFs return 404 after site migration), economy.gov.lb and bdl.gov.lb (403), pcm.gov.lb, mot.gov.lb, tra.gov.lb, industry.gov.lb and libnor.gov.lb (connection timeouts), crdp.org HTML pages (403; the PDF downloaded), jo.pcm.gov.lb (Official Gazette, subscription login). mitai.gov.lb is a JavaScript app; its Public Consultations and Knowledge Hub pages list the National AI Framework, AI Readiness Framework, Cloud Policy Framework, Cyber Readiness Framework and an AI Law as 'coming soon' or 'proposed' with no downloadable text (recorded as leads). Not recorded: the Lebanese University Faculty of Law 'Guidelines on Governance and Ethics of AI in Lebanon' (academic, not a government instrument); MITAI news items and MoUs (press releases); the 2019 National Cyber Security Strategy (no AI content located and no official copy online). The 2019 Ministry of Industry AI strategy exists only as an ESCWA-hosted copy (lead). UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI applies through the UNESCO regional file. No subnational pass needed.

instruments.english_title: Law No. 81 of 10 October 2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data
instruments.current_status: Law No. 81 dated 10 October 2018, published in Official Gazette No. 45 of 18 October 2018; the single article states it enters into force three months after publication (effective date computed from that rule). Full text (47 pp. PDF) served by the Parliament law database (session of 24-25 September 2018). MITAI's 2026 roadmap says a new data protection law has been drafted for Council of Ministers review.
instruments.summary: Lebanon's general law on electronic writing and signatures, e-commerce, the .lb domain and personal data. Book V sets the personal-data rules for all automated and non-automated processing: collection for lawful, specific purposes, data-subject rights and controller duties. Article 86 gives everyone the right to know and contest the logic used in automated processing invoked against them, and bars judicial or administrative decisions that evaluate a person's conduct from resting solely on automated processing aimed at profiling.

instruments.current_status: Slide-deck roadmap: 'Shared - May 15, 2025; Updated - March 05, 2026'. Issued by the Office of the Minister of State for Technology and AI (H.E. Dr. Kamal Shehadi); the document says the office becomes a full ministry once the MITAI law is approved by Parliament. No Council of Ministers adoption is stated in the document. Linked from the MITAI website (LEAP - Path to 2030).
instruments.summary: MITAI's five-year LEAP roadmap for an 'AI-first government' by 2030, built on four tracks: governance foundations, digital and AI infrastructure, talent, and investment. It proposes a Digital & AI Authority reporting to the Prime Minister, a Cybersecurity Institute and an independent telecom and digital regulator, and lists 2025 outputs: the MITAI and Digital Authority laws before Parliament, draft data protection, cybersecurity and e-signature laws, and a National AI Framework and AI Readiness Framework under consultation.

instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated June 2025 on the cover; uploaded to crdp.org in October 2025 (PDF created 7 October 2025). Issued by CRDP, the public curriculum body; the document does not state ministerial approval.
instruments.summary: Sets an AI policy for Lebanese schools plus AI competency frameworks for students and teachers. Schools must keep teacher judgment in final assessments, not let AI determine grades, comply with Law 81/2018, tell parents and students when AI is used, audit tools for bias, require students to cite AI-generated content and train teachers before classroom use. It builds on UNESCO's 2024 AI competency frameworks and the 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of AI.

instruments.english_title: Empowering Lebanon's Healthcare System: A Vision for Digital Health Transformation (Digital Health Vision)
instruments.current_status: Dated July 2023, with a foreword by Minister of Public Health Dr. Firass Abiad. The AI ethical guidelines it announces were not found published.
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Public Health's digital health vision for EHRs, telehealth, interoperability and data governance. Its governance pillar commits to comprehensive ethical guidelines for responsible use of emerging technologies including AI and machine learning in health, developed with OMSAR, with emphasis on transparency, fairness and accountability and reference to WHO guidance on AI ethics in health.
